launch-wa-seattle-discovery-park.description: West Point Lighthouse and South Beach require a substantial walk for most visitors; the beach lot is reserved for ADA placards.
The Loop Trail crosses meadow, forest, and Magnolia Bluff viewpoints, with grades, mud, and exposed weather varying by section.
Daybreak Star Indian Cultural Center is a living cultural destination near the North Lot with its own programs, hours, and visitor expectations.
North, East, and South lots serve different parts of the 560-acre park; general parking is not allowed at the beach.
Discovery Park's play area is near developed park facilities rather than the remote lighthouse and beach zone.

launch-wa-seattle-green-lake-park.description: The 2.8-mile inner loop is a busy paved circuit with pedestrians inside and one-way wheeled users outside at a 10 mph limit.
East Beach sits by the Community Center, Evans Pool, wading pool, playground, and seasonal lifeguarded swim area.
West Green Lake Beach is the longer-season 2026 lifeguarded beach, near Seattle Public Theatre and west-side paths.
The play area and weather-dependent wading pool are the central family zone, operating on separate summer schedules.
The Small Craft Center and hand-carry access support scheduled boating and lake recreation with separate program rules.

launch-wa-seattle-gas-works-park.description: Kite Hill and its sundial provide the signature skyline view and open slope, with wind, wet grass, and event crowds.
The Play Barn is the designated play destination among preserved industrial structures; not all machinery is climbable.
The towers and Great Mound preserve the former gasification plant as landscape and art, with barriers around restricted structures.
The Lake Union viewpoint and picnic lawn overlook the water, but all swimming, wading, fishing, and launching are prohibited.
The Burke-Gilman Trail passes the parking lot and provides the most practical bicycle connection to Fremont and Wallingford.

launch-wa-seattle-seward-park.description: The seasonal lifeguarded beach is near the main developed recreation area, with water-quality and summer-schedule checks required.
Shore Loop Road forms a paved 2.4-mile circuit around the peninsula for walking and cycling beside Lake Washington.
Interior trails enter a rare old-growth forest with roots, hills, mud, wildlife, and fewer facilities than the shoreline loop.
The playground and amphitheater occupy the main activity zone near picnic space, parking, beach access, and special events.

launch-wa-seattle-washington-park-arbore.description: Graham Visitors Center is the orientation point for maps, gift shop, Azalea Way, and exterior restrooms open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Azalea Way is the Arboretum's broad central path and seasonal-flower corridor, connecting major collections north to south.
Pacific Connections Garden is a southern collection area with a bus turnaround, restroom access, lawns, and paths.
The Waterfront Trail explores wetland edges and islands with boardwalks, seasonal water, mud, and wildlife habitat.
Seattle Japanese Garden is a separately ticketed south-end attraction with its own hours, rules, and dog restrictions.

launch-wa-seattle-volunteer-park.description: Volunteer Park Conservatory is a separately operated historic glasshouse with admission, plant collections, and its own hours.
Seattle Asian Art Museum is a separately operated museum inside the park with admission, exhibitions, and event schedules.
The playground and wading pool form the primary family zone; the pool opens only on suitable warm summer days.
The water tower and reservoir are major landmarks, with observation access and stairs subject to posted conditions.
The amphitheater and surrounding lawns host free and permitted programs that can occupy paths, parking, and gathering space.

launch-wa-seattle-kerry-park.description: The W Highland Drive wall is the classic Space Needle, downtown, Elliott Bay, ferry, and weather-dependent Mount Rainier overlook.
Changing Form is the steel sculpture framing the view near the overlook wall and crowded photography area.
Bayview-Kinnear play area is downhill from the main overlook and requires a separate steep neighborhood approach.
West Highland Drive is a narrow residential arrival with no dedicated lot, limited curb space, and frequent rideshare and tour traffic.

launch-wa-seattle-olympic-sculpture-park.description: The main zigzag path crosses the park's grade changes among monumental outdoor sculptures, lawns, trains, and water views.
PACCAR Pavilion is the upper arrival and staffed indoor facility, with restrooms and access tied to separate building hours.
The Elliott Bay pocket beach adds shoreline habitat below the art park; it is not a guarded swimming beach.
The north waterfront trail continues directly into Myrtle Edwards Park and onward toward Centennial Park.

launch-wa-seattle-waterfront-park.description: Overlook Walk is the elevated pedestrian connection between Pike Place Market and the waterfront, with views, stairs, ramps, and elevators.
Pier 58 is the family play destination with a large jellyfish-inspired climbing structure beside the aquarium and promenade.
Pier 62 provides free games, programs, restrooms, furniture, fishing, and a public floating dock during park hours.
Habitat Beach and the promenade reveal restored shoreline habitat beside a heavily traveled urban waterfront.
The Pike Place connection uses Overlook Walk and nearby elevators; meeting at a named entrance prevents confusion across levels.

launch-wa-seattle-golden-gardens-park.description: The lower beach and bathhouse zone provides sand, picnic space, restrooms, volleyball, trains, and Olympic Mountain sunsets.
Installed fire pits are seasonal and first-come; 2026 use runs May 22 through September 7 unless a burn ban applies.
The fishing pier and boat-launch area sit at the south end with cold water, working vessels, and activity-specific rules.
The children's play area is near the lower beach facilities, but dogs are prohibited from both playground and beach.
The one-acre off-leash dog area and forest trail are in the upper northern park, separate from the beach and lower lots.
